| | |
|---|---|
| Branch | `feat/market-leader` (from `qa/full-testing` @ `cf6e65c`) |
| Date | 2026-10-31 |
| Scope | Read-only analysis. **Nothing was built in this phase.** |
| Generated data | [route-matrix.csv](route-matrix.csv) (248 routes) · [model-scope.csv](model-scope.csv) (51 models), regenerated by [`tools/route-matrix.mjs`](tools/route-matrix.mjs) and [`tools/model-scope.py`](tools/model-scope.py) |

## Summary

Of the **64 items** in Phases 1–12, **3 exist**, **33 are partial** and **28 are missing**.

The product is strong on day-to-day POS: billing/GST, KOT, tables, delivery dispatch, inventory recipes, loyalty/khata, attendance, reports and offline billing. It's weakest on:
- **database-level safety:** no RLS; jobs are in-process; no outbox; no idempotency keys; tab split isn't atomic;
- **money control:** no refunds/credit notes, cash shifts or approval PINs;
- **the canteen/institution and sales-channel features that would differentiate it** in the market;
- **the SaaS layer:** plans, billing, self-serve signup, i18n.

**No P0 found in this phase.** I spot-checked every by-id lookup on outlet-level models (orders, payments, KOTs, deliveries, tables, transfers, attendance, reservations) for a missing outlet filter. All are scoped, either in the query or by an outlet check right after loading. The full automated isolation matrix is Phase 1 work. Until it runs, isolation for 40 of 51 models rests on application code alone (see "Models").

## 2. Route × permission × module matrix

The full matrix is in [route-matrix.csv](route-matrix.csv), with one row per route: method + path, file, auth, outlet scope, platform-only, permissions, modules, roles allowed. Summary of the **248 route handlers**:

| Module (from permission → module map) | Routes |
|---|---|
| Inventory | 58 |
| Always on (auth, staff, outlets, settings, notifications, platform, admin, uploads, tax rates) | 57 |
| Billing | 46 |
| Delivery | 31 |
| Tables | 24 |
| Attendance | 15 |
| Customers | 15 |
| Offers | 14 |
| Reports | 9 (+ one dynamic route per report key) |
| Reservations | 8 |
| Kitchen (KOT) | 3 |

| Role | Routes its permissions allow |
|---|---|
| Business Owner | 229 |
| Outlet Manager | 227 |
| Cashier | 108 |
| Inventory | 87 |
| Kitchen | 60 |
| Delivery | 45 |
| Super Admin | 50 by permission, but every outlet route refuses it. Effective access: 9 platform routes + backups, audit (platform-only), GLOBAL settings, uploads, own notifications. |

**Public (no login), 8 routes, all expected:**
- `POST /auth/login`, `/auth/otp/request`, `/auth/otp/verify`, `/auth/refresh`, `/auth/logout`;
- `GET /public/receipts/:token` (signed token);
- `POST /webhooks/razorpay` (signature-verified);
- `GET /uploads/files/:name` (unguessable names; needed for receipts and menus).

**Logged in but no route-level permission, 24 routes.** None leaks data:
- Own data only: notifications (8), `attendance/me/status`, `attendance/calendar` (self unless `attendance:manage`), `attendance/leaves` (self unless manage + scope), `outlets` / `outlets/current` / shifts (the user's own outlets), `tax-rates` (the business's own).
- Uploads: `POST /uploads/image`, `GET /uploads/signature`.
- **Guarded inside the handler:** `GET /delivery/:id`, `PATCH /delivery/:id/status`, `POST /delivery/:id/{collect,complete,issue,upi-qr,upi-qr/:paymentId/confirm}` all call `canSee` / `assertMyDelivery`, which allows the manager or the assigned partner only.
- **Recommendation (Phase 1):** move these to explicit route-level guards so the matrix can be checked mechanically.

## 3. Models and tenancy

The full list is in [model-scope.csv](model-scope.csv): **51 models**.

| Group | Count | Models | Isolation today |
|---|---|---|---|
| `businessId` + auto-filtered by the tenant extension | 11 | Outlet, User, MenuCategory, MenuItem, Customer, InventoryItem, Vendor, Offer, Coupon, TaxRate, AuditLog | Every query filtered in the Prisma extension |
| `businessId` column, not auto-filtered | 0 | — | — |
| `outletId` only | 21 | Order, KotTicket, StaffAttendance, Shift-linked rows, Delivery, DeliveryZone, DeliveryCashHandover, DiningArea, DiningTable, TableSession, Reservation, InventoryStock, InventoryTransaction, Purchase, StockAudit, KhataTransaction, Notification (outletId nullable), ReportSchedule, OutletItemOverride, … | Route code must filter by `req.outletId` (validated against the user's outlets) |
| Neither (child or global rows) | 19 | Business; via parent: OrderItem, Payment, ItemVariant, ItemAddon, TableSessionItem, LoyaltyTransaction, CouponRedemption, Recipe, PurchaseItem, PurchasePayment, StockAuditLine, StockTransfer (from/to outlet), StockTransferItem, LeaveRequest, RefreshToken, DeviceToken; global: OtpCode, Setting (scope = businessId / outletId / GLOBAL) | Reached only through a scoped parent |

**Implication for Phase 1 RLS:** 40 of 51 tables have no `businessId` column. Simple, fast RLS policies need a `businessId` column on each business-owned table, added nullable, backfilled in batches, then made NOT NULL. Policies that join through Outlet are slower. See Decision D10.

## 6. Proposed order

The brief's order is mostly right. These are my proposed changes, for you to confirm:

1. **Phase 1 additions:** the missing indexes (above), and moving the in-handler delivery guards to route level. Both are low-risk and help everything later.
2. **Phase 1 sequencing inside the phase:**
   - indexes;
   - `businessId` backfill on outlet-level tables;
   - RLS **in "permissive + logging" mode first**, then enforce;
   - outbox (also used by jobs);
   - pg-boss worker;
   - idempotency keys;
   - atomic tab split;
   - Redis adapter behind config;
   - backups off-site plus a restore drill;
   - observability.
3. **Phase 3 before Phase 2's heavier items**, if you want pilot hotels sooner. Refunds/credit notes, cash shifts and approval PINs matter more day to day than TOTP. I recommend keeping 2.2 (reset link), 2.3 (PIN lockout, sessions) and 2.8 inside Phase 2, and doing Phase 2 → 3 in order as written.
4. **Phase 8.4 (GSTR-1 B2B/credit notes) depends on 3.1** (credit notes) and customer GSTIN capture. It stays in Phase 8, with GSTIN capture added to Phase 3.
5. **Phase 6 (channels) after Phase 5 (canteen).** Canteen is buildable without vendor contracts; channels need vendor decisions (D3) and sandbox access.
6. **Phase 12.5 (Expo SDK upgrade)** as a separate PR any time after Phase 2.7. SDK 51 is behind current store targets, so plan it before any store release.
7. **The QA programme** (`qa/full-testing`, Phases 3–16) continues after you confirm. Its suites (isolation matrix, concurrency, load) are reused as each build phase lands.

| D1 | Coupon/flat-discount GST default: pre-tax (today) vs GST-inclusive | Phase 3 | Keep **pre-tax** as default (current behaviour, matches GST valuation rules for discounts shown on the invoice), and add an outlet setting. Confirm with your CA. |
| D2 | Aadhaar: full encrypted (today), last-4 only, or per-hotel opt-in | Phase 2 | **Last-4 + consent record by default**; full encrypted number only when the hotel opts in. Existing full numbers kept but re-confirmed, or reduced to last-4 by a migration you approve. |
| D3 | Aggregators: hub partner vs direct APIs; which vendors first | Phase 6 | **Hub partner** (e.g. UrbanPiper-style) first: one integration covers Zomato and Swiggy. Direct partner APIs need approval per brand. |
| D4 | Queue: pg-boss vs BullMQ/Redis | Phase 1 | **pg-boss** (no new infrastructure; Postgres already there). Redis only if the Socket.io adapter (1.5) is enabled. |
| D5 | Payment gateway for subscriptions and wallets | Phase 5 / 11 | **Razorpay** (already integrated for UPI QR); mock adapter first. |
| D6 | Wallet/gift-card scope and RBI PPI implications | Phase 3.8 / 5.2 | Start with a **closed-loop** wallet (usable only at that hotel / institution). Closed-loop PPIs are exempt from RBI authorisation. No cash-out, no transfers. Confirm with counsel. |
| D7 | Face-recognition clock-in | Phase 2.6 | **Design only**; build selfie capture (stored, no matching) + mock-location detection. |
| D8 | Languages beyond Tamil/Hindi | Phase 11 | Tamil + Hindi first; framework ready for Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi. |
| D9 | Hotel room management | Phase 7.4 | **Out of scope**; build bill-to-room as a folio reference only. |

Additional decisions from recon:

| # | Decision | Needed before | My recommendation |
|---|---|---|---|
| D10 | RLS design: add `businessId` to the 40 tables without it (nullable → batch backfill → NOT NULL), vs policies that join through Outlet | Phase 1 | **Add `businessId` columns.** Simpler, faster policies; also speeds up reports. |
| D11 | Feature-flag mechanism: reuse the 10 modules, or a new per-hotel `features` map that the Super Admin toggles | Phase 1 | **New `features` map** for capabilities (default OFF for existing hotels); modules stay for what a hotel pays for. Flags declare which modules they require. |
| D12 | Worker hosting: pg-boss needs a second always-on process (a Render **Background Worker**, extra cost) | Phase 1 | Yes, a separate worker service, plus an env switch to run the worker inside the API for small installs. |
| D13 | Owner reset links (2.2) and 2FA SMS fallback need a configured email (SMTP) **or** SMS (MSG91) in production | Phase 2 | Require at least one in production; in development, links are logged. |
| D14 | Features you asked for on 2026-10-31 (auto out-of-stock, bills filters, WhatsApp, branding) are live **without flags**. Should auto out-of-stock go behind a flag (ON for Demo Hotel, OFF for other existing hotels) to follow rule 5? | Phase 1 | **Yes, flag it**, ON for Demo Hotel. Keep bills filters and branding unflagged (UI only, no rule change). WhatsApp is already opt-in per hotel. |
| D15 | Scope: 12 phases is several months of work. Which phases are needed for your first pilot hotels? | now | **Pilot set: Phases 1, 2, 3, 4** + indexes. Then 5 (canteen) as the differentiator, 9 (performance) before scaling, then 6/7/8/10/11/12. |
| D16 | Web session storage: move tokens from localStorage to httpOnly cookies (needs a same-site API domain, e.g. `api.yourdomain` + `app.yourdomain`, plus CSRF protection) | Phase 2 | Yes, with custom domains on Vercel/Render (already in the deployment guide). |

| Bluetooth/LAN ESC/POS printing, cash drawer | Need hardware | Manual hardware checklist |
